links.outcome: Whether models abandon correct diagnoses when given incorrect advice, clinician versus lay framing
links.effect: Clinician-framed misleading advice produced lower final accuracy than lay-framed advice in every model, with differences of 4.6 to 38.2 percentage points.
links.quote: Clinician-framed misleading advice produced lower final accuracy than lay-framed advice in every model, with differences of 4.6 to 38.2 percentage points.

links.outcome: Accuracy with versus without answer options in multi-turn diagnostic conversations
links.effect: Average accuracy was 76.9% with answer options and 57.0% without them across seven models and 1,035 cases from five datasets.
links.quote: Across seven models and 1,035 cases from five datasets, average accuracy was 76.9% with answer options and 57.0% without them.

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluation of LLM robustness against misleading framing and multi-turn advice during diagnostic conversations, but does not test a health system deployment practice or safeguard.
